structured_output.what_is_happening: "Muse Protocol" ($Protocol) is a 38-minute-old PumpSwap pair at about $85k market cap. The packet lists another "Muse Protocol" token (QwtD…) created about 22 minutes before this one, with $10.1M of volume in the last hour, $302k of liquidity and a $199k market cap. That makes this token a same-name copycat riding the other one's attention. It rose about 750% in the hour after launch but is now down about 23–27% over 5 minutes and about 38% below its all-time high. Sellers now outnumber buyers in the last 5 minutes (91 sells vs 73 buys; 60 unique sellers vs 49 unique buyers). The creator wallet holds 18.6% of supply, the liquidity is 0% locked and 0% burned, and RugCheck flags "Large Amount of LP Unlocked" and "Low amount of LP Providers". The token never went through the pump.fun bonding curve (migrated_unix 0), so the creator probably seeded and controls the pool.

narrative.description: The 'Muse Protocol' story belongs to the earlier token that has far more volume. This token borrows its name and ticker. It has no website, socials or description of its own. GeckoTerminal lists the handle 'museprotocollol', which may just point to the original's account.
narrative.why_spreading: Spillover from the real Muse Protocol token. Buyers searching the name or ticker, and bots, land on the wrong contract. About 2,000 unique buyers against 108 sellers fits mistaken or automated buying more than holders who believe in this token.

token_connection.why_this_token: Only the matching name and ticker. It was created after the leading token and has about 1/40th of that token's hourly volume.
token_connection.competing_tokens: QwtD… (created earlier, $10.1M volume in the last hour, $302k liquidity, $199k market cap) is clearly the canonical one. Gr8x… is another later copycat with almost no volume.

authenticity.evidence: There are no paid boosts, no alert or call-channel counts, no bundlers, no snipers and a bot/degen rate of 0. However, the creator is the largest holder at 18.6% (GMGN tags it as a rat trader), the creator appears to control unlocked LP, and the buyer/seller asymmetry looks like confused, name-driven buying rather than organic interest in this contract.
authenticity.uncertainty: I cannot see X posts or wallet flows. The creator wallet shows no launch history, which could be a fresh wallet set up for this.

structural_risks: LP is 0% locked or burned, and the creator appears to be the main liquidity provider, so the liquidity can be pulled at any time
The creator holds 18.6% of supply and can dump it into about $59k of liquidity
It is a copycat of a much larger token with the same name, so attention will move to the real one
Momentum has already turned: down about 38% from the high and sellers outnumber buyers over the last 5 minutes
Doubling from entry would need about $170k+ market cap, which competes directly with the original at $199k

structured_output.counterargument: About 2,000 unique buyers is a large, spread-out holder base, and the creator has not sold yet (status creator_hold). If the original Muse Protocol keeps running hard, spillover demand could lift copycats again, and a $60k pool relative to an $85k market cap means big moves in either direction. Some copycats trade as 'beta' plays on the original for a few hours.

structured_output.thesis: This is a late same-name copycat of a much larger Muse Protocol token. The creator holds 18.6% of supply and the liquidity is unlocked and likely creator-supplied. The price is already fading from its spike. A 2x before a -50% move or a liquidity pull is unlikely, and a pull or slow death within 6 hours is the most likely outcome.
